questions.question: In the following sets, which set represents the sides of a right-angled triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled triangle, the lengths of the sides must form a valid Pythagorean triplet.

Standard Pythagorean triplets frequently asked in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

By direct observation, the set {5, 12, 13} exactly matches a standard Pythagorean triplet.

**∴ The correct answer is {5, 12, 13}.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Options with sets of side lengths: {3, 4, 6}, {8, 15, 16}, {5, 10, 12}, and {5, 12, 13}

**Formula Used:**

According to the Pythagoras Theorem, for a triangle to be right-angled, the sum of the squares of the two smaller sides must be equal to the square of the longest side (hypotenuse):

a² + b² = c²

 

 
 Base = 12
 Height = 5
 Hypotenuse = 13

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's check Option 1: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25. The square of the third side is 6² = 36. Since 25 ≠ 36, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 2: 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289. The square of the third side is 16² = 256. Since 289 ≠ 256, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 3: 5² + 10² = 25 + 100 = 125. The square of the third side is 12² = 144. Since 125 ≠ 144, it is not a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Let's check Option 4: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169. The square of the third side is 13² = 169. Since 169 = 169, it perfectly satisfies the theorem.

**∴ The correct answer is {5, 12, 13}.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is exactly equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Some basic integer triplets to memorize are (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (9, 40, 41). Any constant multiple of these triplets (e.g., 6, 8, 10) also forms a right-angled triangle.

Identifying Triangle Types

If c is the longest side: If a² + b² > c², the triangle is an acute-angled triangle. If a² + b² < c², the triangle is an obtuse-angled triangle.

questions.question: If the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is 25 : 144, the ratio of their corresponding sides is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their corresponding sides is simply the square root of the ratio of their areas.

Ratio of sides = √(Area₁ / Area₂)

⇒ Ratio of sides = √(25 / 144)

⇒ Ratio of sides = 5 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of areas of two similar triangles (A₁ : A₂) = 25 : 144

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is strictly equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

A₁ / A₂ = (S₁ / S₂)²

 Ratio of Areas = S₁² : S₂²

 
 

 A₁ = 25
 
 

 

 

 S₁

 
 

 A₂ = 144
 
 

 

 

 S₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ (S₁ / S₂)² = 25 / 144

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = √(25 / 144)

⇒ S₁ / S₂ = 5 / 12

**∴ The correct answer is 5 : 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

When two triangles are similar, their corresponding interior angles are exactly equal, and the ratio of their corresponding side lengths remains constant.

Perimeters and Altitudes Ratio

The ratio of perimeters, corresponding altitudes, angle bisectors, and medians of two similar triangles is strictly equivalent to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Volumes of Similar Figures

For any three-dimensional similar geometric shapes, the ratio of their total volumes is equal to the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear 1D dimensions.

questions.question: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 7 : 8 : 3, then the value of the largest angle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The largest angle of a triangle corresponds to the largest part in the given ratio.

Total parts = 7 + 8 + 3 = 18 parts

Largest part = 8

Largest angle = (8 ÷ 18) × 180° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The angles of the triangle are in the ratio 7 : 8 : 3.

Let the three angles of the triangle be 7x, 8x, and 3x.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

 

 
 

 

 

 
 7x
 8x
 3x

 A
 B
 C

**Calculations:**

⇒ 7x + 8x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 18x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 18

⇒ x = 10°

⇒ The largest angle corresponds to the largest ratio part, which is 8x.

⇒ Largest angle = 8 × 10° = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of a Triangle

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180°. This fundamental property helps determine unknown angles when given in ratios or expressions.

Types of Triangles Based on Angles

An acute triangle has all angles less than 90°, a right triangle has exactly one 90° angle, and an obtuse triangle has one angle greater than 90°. The triangle in this problem is acute since its angles are 70°, 80°, and 30°.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two opposite interior remote angles.
</p

questions.question: Two of the angles of a scalene triangle are 40° and 62°. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two angles of a scalene triangle: 40° and 62°

**Formula:**

The sum of the interior angles of a triangle = 180°

Calculation:

To find the measure of the third angle, we need to subtract the measures of the two given angles from 180°:

Sum of the two given angles = 40° + 62°

= 102°

Third angle = 180° - Sum of the two given angles

= 180° - 102°

= 78°

**So, the measure of the third angle is 78°.**

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. The difference in the largest and smallest angle is (in degrees):
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts.

Difference in ratio parts between the largest and smallest angle = 3 − 1 = 2 parts.

Sum of interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

Required difference = (2 ÷ 6) × 180° = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of the three angles of a triangle is 1 : 2 : 3.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles in a triangle = 180°

 
 

 
 
 

 1x (Smallest)
 
 
 

 3x (Largest)
 
 
 

 2x
 
 
 1x + 2x + 3x = 180°

**Calculations:**

Let the three angles of the triangle be x, 2x, and 3x.

⇒ x + 2x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 6x = 180°

⇒ x = 30°

The smallest angle = x = 30°

The largest angle = 3x = 3 × 30° = 90°

⇒ Difference between the largest and smallest angle = 90° − 30° = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Angles Property

The sum of all three interior angles of a planar triangle is always exactly 180° regardless of the triangle's shape or dimensions.

Right-Angled Triangle

Since the largest angle in this specific triangle is exactly 90°, it forms a right-angled triangle where the sum of the two remaining acute angles is also 90°.

Polygon Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon, including a triangle, the sum of its exterior angles (taking one at each vertex) is always exactly 360°.
</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since AB = AC, the triangle is isosceles and angles opposite to equal sides are equal (∠B = ∠C).

∠B = (180º − ∠A) ÷ 2

∠B = (180º − 80º) ÷ 2 = 100º ÷ 2 = 50º

**∴ The correct answer is 50º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In ΔABC, AB = AC

∠A = 80º

•

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles of a triangle is 180º.

Angles opposite to equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.

**Calculation:**

⇒ In ΔABC, AB = AC

⇒ Therefore, ∠B = ∠C

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 80º + ∠B + ∠B = 180º

⇒ 2 × ∠B = 180º − 80º

⇒ 2 × ∠B = 100º

⇒ ∠B = 100º ÷ 2

⇒ ∠B = 50º

**∴ The correct answer is 50º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Properties

A triangle with two equal sides is an isosceles triangle. The angles opposite to the equal sides are always equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any triangle is always equal to 180º.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles: ∠Ext = ∠Int₁ + ∠Int₂.

questions.question: In ΔPQR, angle bisector of ∠P intersects QR at M. If PQ = PR, then what is the value of ∠PMQ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔPQR, angle bisector of ∠P intersects QR at M.

PQ = PR

**Concept Used:**

When two sides of a triangle are equal then the triangle is isosceles and and angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d2f9e34bb1085ba6935243e597bbff6f0fa81d71c942df8ebaaf7cb45ac6a0ec.png] 

In ΔPQR, PQ = PR

⇒ ∠Q = ∠R = b

PM is the angle bisector of ∠P.

∠QPM = ∠RPM = a

In ΔPQR, apply Angle Sum Property

∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180° 

∠P + b + b = 180° 

∠P = 180° - 2b

∠QPM = (180° - 2b)/2 = 90° - b

In ΔPQM

Let ∠PMQ = θ

∠QPM + ∠Q + ∠M = 180° 

90 - b + b + θ = 180° 

θ = 180° - 90° 

θ = 90° 

**∠PMQ = 90° **

questions.question: In triangle PQR , S and T are the midpoints of the sides PQ and PR, respectively. The length of the side QR is 12 cm. If ST is parallel to QR, then find the length (in cm) of ST.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the Midpoint Theorem, the line segment joining the midpoints of any two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is equal to half of its length.

Since S and T are the midpoints of sides PQ and PR respectively, ST is parallel to QR.

Length of ST = QR ÷ 2

Length of ST = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In triangle PQR, S and T are the midpoints of the sides PQ and PR respectively.

The length of the side QR = 12 cm.

ST is parallel to QR.

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal.

Midpoint property: PS = PQ ÷ 2 and PT = PR ÷ 2.

**Calculations:**

⇒ In triangle PST and triangle PQR, angle P is common.

⇒ Since ST is parallel to QR, corresponding angles are equal: angle PST = angle PQR.

⇒ Therefore, triangle PST is similar to triangle PQR (by AA similarity criterion).

⇒ The ratio of corresponding sides will be equal: ST / QR = PS / PQ

⇒ Since S is the midpoint of PQ, the ratio of PS to PQ is 1 / 2.

⇒ ST / 12 = 1 / 2

⇒ ST = 12 × (1 / 2)

⇒ ST = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is always parallel to the third side and is exactly half of its length.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, then it divides the two sides proportionally in the same ratio.

Properties of Similar Triangles

When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their corresponding sides is equal, and the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

questions.question: △ABC and △RPQ are congruent, then the side of △ABC that corresponds to PQ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two triangles are given as congruent, the order of their letters directly shows the corresponding parts.

For ▵ABC ≅ ▵RPQ, simply match the positions of the letters.

The letters P and Q are at the second and third positions in RPQ.

The letters at the second and third positions in ABC are B and C.

Therefore, side PQ corresponds to side BC.

**∴ The correct answer is BC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

▵ABC ≅ ▵RPQ

**Concept Used:**

Two triangles are congruent if their corresponding sides and angles are equal in measure. The sequence of the vertices in the congruence statement specifies the exactly matched parts.

 
 

 A
 B
 C

 P
 Q

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 

 
 Corresponding Sides: BC & PQ

⇒ Based on the congruency statement ▵ABC ≅ ▵RPQ, we establish the following exact vertex correspondence:

⇒ Vertex A corresponds to Vertex R

⇒ Vertex B corresponds to Vertex P

⇒ Vertex C corresponds to Vertex Q

⇒ The side formed by connecting vertices P and Q in ▵RPQ naturally corresponds to the matching vertices in ▵ABC.

⇒ Since P → B and Q → C, the side PQ corresponds to the side BC.

**∴ The correct answer is BC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CPCTC Theorem

CPCTC stands for "Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent". It simply implies that once you have proven two triangles are congruent, all of their corresponding angles and sides are equal.

Conditions for Congruency

Two triangles can be proven congruent using five major geometric criteria: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

Similarity vs Congruence

Congruent triangles have the exact same shape and size (ratio of sides is exactly 1). Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size, meaning their corresponding angles are equal, but corresponding sides are only proportional.
</p

questions.question: If ∆ABC ~ ∆DEF, and BC = 4 cm, EF = 5 cm and the area of triangle ABC = 80 cm² , then the area of the triangle DEF is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∆ABC ~ ∆DEF, and BC = 4 cm, EF = 5 cm and the area of triangle ABC = 80 cm².

**Concept used:**

In two similar triangles, 

Ratio of their area is equal to ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

Area of ∆ABC : Area of ∆DEF = BC² : EF²

⇒80 : Area of ∆DEF = 4² : 5²

⇒Area of ∆DEF = 25 × 80/16

⇒Area of ∆DEF = 125

**Hence, The Required value is 125 cm².**

questions.question: The area of two similar triangles XYZ and ABC are 361 cm² and 225 cm², respectively. If the longest side of the larger ∆XYZ be 38 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the longest side of the smaller ∆ABC?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∆XYZ and ∆ ABC are similar triangles

Area of ∆XYZ = 361 cm²

Area of ∆ ABC = 225 cm² 

**Concept used:**

If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

**Calculations:**

Let the longest side of ∆ ABC be x cm.

According to the question,

The ∆XYZ and ∆ABC are similar, 

Thus we have, (area(∆XYZ))/(area(∆ABC))= ((longest side of ∆XYZ)²)/((longest side of ∆ABC)²)

⇒ (361)/(225) = (38²)/(x²)

⇒ x² = (38² × 225)/(361)

⇒ x² = 900

⇒ x = √900 = 30

**Hence, The length of the longest side of ∆ABC is 30 cm.**

questions.question:
If the figure, AB = AD = 7 cm and AC = AE and BC = 11 cm, then find the length of ED.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d9257ba81ef22dd3366e697ac6a0b7adddb56061b1d733964d867d144ce052d.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = AD = 7 cm and AC = AE and BC = 11 cm

**Concept Used:**

According to the concept of similarity, two triangles are said to be similar if two sides of one triangle are in the same ratio as two sides of the other triangle and the angle subtended by the two sides in both triangles is equal.

**Calculation:**

Since AB = AD, and AC = AE, by concept,

ΔABC ∼ ΔADE

Therefore, AB/AD = BC/ED = AC/AE

Now, AB/AD = BC/ED

⇒ 1 = 11/ED (∵ AB = AD)

⇒ ED = 11

**∴ The length of ED is 11 cm.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. A triangle can have all angles less than 60°.

B. A triangle can have one obtuse angle.

C. A triangle can have two right angles.

D. A triangle can have two acute angles.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Options regarding the properties of triangles:

A. A triangle can have all angles less than 60º.

B. A triangle can have one obtuse angle.

C. A triangle can have two right angles.

D. A triangle can have two acute angles.

**Concept:**

In a triangle:

The sum of all angles is always 180º.

An obtuse angle is greater than 90º.

A right angle is exactly 90º.

An acute angle is less than 90º.

**Calculation:**

**Statement A:** A triangle can have all angles less than 60º.

&rA
